gen-dafont-ozone-gf-cambo: Ozone's stems and crossbars look drawn with a compass pencil, every round form ending in a wide-set curve. Ozone stays rigid and technical, while Cambo swings mellowly from heavy to light.
gen-dafont-ozone-gf-noto-serif-gujarati: Technical and geometric, Ozone gives curves and straights a single width, with capitals hardly standing apart from the lowercase. Noto Serif Gujarati brings bookish authority, and that gap in temperament is what the pair does best.
gen-dafont-ozone-gf-noto-serif-lao: Technical to the core, Ozone holds one constant pen width through every stroke, capitals barely above the lowercase. And Noto Serif Lao handles the softer job, its lightly tilted nib variation shaping bowls with gentle shifts.
gen-dafont-ozone-gf-noto-serif-makasar: Ozone sets a gentle monotone of line, stems and crossbars alike, with wide-set curve ends in its round forms. Noto Serif Makasar steps in with a towering x-height, soft heavy-to-light strokes, warming what Ozone starts.
gen-dafont-ozone-gf-noto-serif-ottoman-s: Ozone's strokes look like bent copper pipe, tubular and geometric all the way. Noto Serif Ottoman Siyaq adds dignified bowls that swell only slightly, and that pipe-versus-pen tension is the best thing here.
gen-dafont-ozone-gf-noto-serif-sinhala: Noto Serif Sinhala stacks a tall band of letters beneath short stalks, with stroke weights that differ just enough to feel alive. Beneath Ozone's uniform lines, text would read refined and bookish, line after line.
gen-dafont-ozone-gf-noto-serif-telugu: Traditional and refined in feel, the body text follows Ozone's thread-like strokes with a gentle weight shift. Noto Serif Telugu keeps its stems a shade heavier than connecting arms, so lines glide along nearly capital-high letters.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-fs-plein: Plakkaat bends its lines like straw, terminals curling nearly back to the stem. Plein opens a clear channel into each round letter, so reading flows with a reliable, clean ease.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-bree-serif: Plakkaat looks traced with a marker, bold and heavy, with terminals nearly touching. Bree Serif does the quieter job, its outsized lowercase giving literary refinement where Plakkaat gives sheer weight.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-outfit: Heavy and shut tight: Plakkaat's closed letters curl nearly into the stem, while Outfit leaves its curves open. Beside each other, one clenches while the other breathes out, approachable and clean.
